extraction.name: MMStar
extraction.description: MMStar is an elite vision-indispensable multi-modal benchmark comprising 1,500 samples meticulously selected by humans. It benchmarks 6 core capabilities (Coarse Perception, Fine-grained Perception, Instance Reasoning, Logical Reasoning, Science & Technology, Mathematics) and 18 detailed axes, aiming to evaluate LVLMs' multi-modal capacities with carefully balanced and purified samples that exhibit visual dependency, minimal data leakage, and require advanced multi-modal capabilities.
extraction.creator: Lin Chen, Jinsong Li, Xiaoyi Dong, Pan Zhang, Yuhang Zang, Zehui Chen, Haodong Duan, Jiaqi Wang, Yu Qiao, Dahua Lin, Feng Zhao (University of Science and Technology of China, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shanghai AI Laboratory)
extraction.citeAs: Chen, L., Li, J., Dong, X., Zhang, P., Zang, Y., Chen, Z., Duan, H., Wang, J., Qiao, Y., Lin, D., & Zhao, F. (2024). Are We on the Right Way for Evaluating Large Vision-Language Models? arXiv:2403.20330v2 [cs.CV].
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Samples were first roughly selected from existing multi-modal benchmarks (SEED, AI2D, ScienceQA, MMBench, MathVista, MMMU) using an automated pipeline with LLM inspectors to filter out visually unnecessary or leaked samples, followed by strict manual review by three experts to curate 1,500 high-quality multimodal evaluation samples.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Samples collected from six existing multi-modal benchmarks: SEED-Image, AI2D-Test, ScienceQA-Test, MMBench-EN-Dev, MathVista-Mini, and MMMU-Val, starting from a pool of 22,401 samples.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Samples were transformed from uni-modal to multi-modal formats where necessary to prevent LLMs from recalling correct answers. Difficulty levels were assigned based on hit counts from 16 LVLMs: easy (12-16 hits), moderate (8-11), hard (4-7), and tough (0-3).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: An automated coarse filtering pipeline was applied using two closed-source LLMs (GPT4-Turbo, GeminiPro) and six open-source LLMs (sizing 20B or larger) as inspectors with 2-shot in-context inference. Samples with hit counts of more than 2 out of 8 LLM inspectors were excluded. This reduced the pool from 22,401 to 11,607 candidate samples. Subsequently, manual review further narrowed the selection to 1,500 final samples, ensuring visual dependency, coverage of capability dimensions, and difficulty diversity.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Three experts conducted manual review to ensure: (1) each sample's answer is based on understanding of visual content; (2) selected samples cover a comprehensive range of capability assessment dimensions; (3) most samples require LVLMs to possess advanced multi-modal abilities for resolution. Samples were split into four difficulty categories based on LVLM hit counts before manual selection.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Difficulty levels were determined by tallying hit counts of 16 LVLMs on coarsely filtered samples. Samples were categorized as easy (12-16 hits), moderate (8-11), hard (4-7), and tough (0-3). LLM inspector hit counts were used to assess visual dependency and data leakage risk.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Three domain experts conducted the manual review process.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Eight LLM inspectors: GPT4-Turbo, GeminiPro (closed-source), LLaMA-70B, Qwen-1.5-72B, Mixtral-8x7B, InternLM2-20B, Yi-34B, Deepseek-67B (open-source). Sixteen LVLMs used for difficulty assessment including GPT4V, GeminiPro-Vision, LLaVA series, and others. VLMEvalKit used as evaluation codebase.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors plan to expand MMStar into a larger, online test set and explore dynamic evaluation methods to maintain sample visual dependency and reduce accidental data leakage into LLM and LVLM training corpora.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: MMStar aims to provide a fairer and more accurate evaluation platform for large vision-language models, helping the research community avoid misjudgments of actual multi-modal capabilities caused by visually unnecessary samples and unintentional data leakage. This could guide more reliable development of LVLMs and prevent misleading conclusions about model capabilities.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The benchmark is sourced predominantly from SEED (28.3% of final 1,500 samples), MMBench (24.4%), MathVista (23.0%), AI2D (13.1%), MMMU (6.7%), and ScienceQA (4.6%), which may reflect the biases present in these source benchmarks. The selection process focused on natural images and scientific/technical knowledge domains.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark is limited to 1,500 samples selected from six existing benchmarks, which may not cover all possible multi-modal evaluation dimensions. The automated filtering relies on LLM inspectors that may themselves have biases. The benchmark is static and may become subject to data leakage over time as new models are trained on larger corpora.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing and evaluation of large vision-language models (LVLMs) on multi-modal capabilities. The benchmark is designed to assess actual multi-modal gains using two proposed metrics: multi-modal gain (MG) and multi-modal leakage (ML). It is intended for benchmarking, not for training or fine-tuning.
